{{Short description|FIFA World Cup group}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2025}}
{{Use American English|date=November 2025}}
Group H of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] took place from June 15 to 26, 2026.<ref name="match schedule">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/1be9ce37eb98fcc5/original/FWC26-Match-Schedule_English.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 26 – Match Schedule |publisher=[[FIFA]] |date=February 4, 2024 |access-date=February 4, 2024}}</ref> The group consisted of [[Spain national football team|Spain]], [[Cape Verde national football team|Cape Verde]], [[Saudi Arabia national football team|Saudi Arabia]], and [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]].

Spain finished at the top of the group with two group game wins, allowing them to advance to the [[2026 FIFA World Cup round of 32|round of 32]], where they defeated multiple teams in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage|knockout stage]] and became champions of this World Cup.

Cape Verde finished as runners-up after drawing all three of its group matches, becoming the first World Cup debutant (and the smallest nation) to advance to the knockout stage since [[Slovakia national football team|Slovakia]] in [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010]].

Uruguay finished third in the group and were eliminated, as their performance meant it would be impossible for them to be among the top eight third-place teams. Saudi Arabia finished fourth based on goal difference, and were also eliminated.<ref name="regulations">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 2026 Regulations |publisher=FIFA |date=May 2025 |access-date=June 7, 2025 |archive-date=June 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623212158/https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Standings==
{{2026 FIFA World Cup group tables|Group H}}

In the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 32|round of 32]]:<ref name="regulations"/>
* The winner of Group H, [[Spain national football team|Spain]], advanced to play the runner-up of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group J|Group J]], [[Austria national football team|Austria]].
* The runner-up of Group H, [[Cape Verde national football team|Cape Verde]], advanced to play the winner of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group J|Group J]], [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]].

==Matches==
All times listed are local.<ref name="match schedule"/>

===Spain vs Cape Verde===
The teams had never met before. The fixture marked Cape Verde's debut at the FIFA World Cup. The country was the second least populated country to qualify for the tournament, before [[Curaçao national football team|Curaçao]] achieved qualification.

In the first half Spain's [[Ferran Torres]] hit the bar with a shot from close range after a header back from [[Marc Cucurella]] on the left. In the second half [[Mikel Oyarzabal]] had a shot blocked by [[Pico Lopes|Pico]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/760428|title= Spain shocked by Cape Verde, draw 0–0 in their World Cup opener|date=15 June 2026|work=ESPN|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref> Late on [[Diney (footballer, born 1995)|Diney]] almost put Cape Verde into the lead when he headed a corner straight at Spanish goalkeeper [[Unai Simón]] with the game finishing 0–0 and producing one of the biggest shocks of the World Cup, with [[Vozinha]] as the Man of the Match for making seven saves in his World Cup debut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cr7xnk3eygxt|title= Spain 0 Cape Verde 0|date=15 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/world-cup-2026/2026/0615/1578606-lopes-stars-as-debutants-cape-verde-claim-famous-draw/|title= Pico Lopes stars as World Cup debutants Cape Verde claim famous draw against Spain|date=15 June 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref>

Cape Verde committed a single foul during this game, the fewest in a FIFA World Cup match since data collection began in 1966.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Tweedale |first1=Ali |title=How Cape Verde Frustrated Spain to Pull Off One of the World Cup's Biggest Ever Shocks |url=https://theanalyst.com/articles/how-cape-verde-frustrated-spain-world-cup-history-draw-shock |access-date=22 July 2026 |work=Opta Analyst |date=15 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Harris |first1=Thom |title=How Cape Verde shocked Spain: One foul, a block defence and tracking runners |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7364332/2026/06/15/cape-verde-spain-draw-analysis/ |access-date=22 July 2026 |work=The New York Times |date=3 July 2026}}</ref>

===Saudi Arabia vs Uruguay===
[[File:Saudi Arabia vs Uruguay. FIFA World Cup 2026. (55339442284).jpg|thumb|right|Pre-match ceremony between Saudi Arabia and Uruguay.]]
The teams had previously faced each other thrice, most recently in [[2018 FIFA World Cup Group A#Uruguay v Saudi Arabia|Uruguay's 1–0 win]] at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Saudi Arabia national football team: record v Uruguay|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/saudi-arabia/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Uruguay|website=11v11.com|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref>

In the 41st minute, Saudi Arabia went in front, [[Hassan Al-Tambakti]]'s header from a corner on the right was parried out by Uruguay keeper [[Fernando Muslera]] where [[Abdulelah Al-Amri]] finished the rebound with his right foot to the net from close range. With ten minutes to go, [[Maximiliano Araújo]] scored for Uruguay with a shot from the left after [[Mohammed Al-Owais]] had initially made a save to make it 1–1, which also became the final result of the affair.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cz75wdgv3jwt|title= Saudi Arabia 1 Uruguay 1|date=15 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=17 June 2026}}</ref>

===Spain vs Saudi Arabia===
The teams had met three times, including their first encounter in [[2006 FIFA World Cup Group H#Saudi Arabia vs Spain|Spain's 1–0 group stage victory]] at the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Spain vs. Saudi Arabia Head-to-Head in the World Cups|url=https://www.thesoccerworldcups.com/head_to_head/spain_vs_saudi_arabia.php|website=The Soccer World Cups|access-date=6 December 2025}}</ref> Spain won all matches, most recently a 5–0 friendly in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=Spain national football team: record v Saudi Arabia|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/spain/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Saudi%20Arabia|website=11v11.com|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref>

The fixture was Saudi Arabia's worst defeat at the World Cup since their [[2018 FIFA World Cup Group A#Russia vs Saudi Arabia|5−0 loss]] to hosts [[Russia national football team|Russia]] in [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]], and their third-largest defeat in tournament history, tied with their 4–0 losses against hosts [[1998 FIFA World Cup Group C#France vs Saudi Arabia|France]] in [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]] and [[2006 FIFA World Cup Group H#Saudi Arabia vs Ukraine|Ukraine]] in [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006]].

===Uruguay vs Cape Verde===
[[File:Cape Verde vs Uruguay 2026.jpg|thumb|right|[[Hard Rock Stadium]] during the match.]]
The two teams had never met before.

In the 21st minute, [[Kevin Pina (footballer)|Kevin Pina]] scored with a low long range right footed free-kick from 30 yards that went through the middle of the defensive wall and into the bottom right corner of the net, it was the first ever goal for Cape Verde in the World Cup Finals. [[Maximiliano Araújo]] made it 1–1 the 44th minute when he dived low to head to the net from close range after [[Sidny Lopes Cabral]] had headed against his own post.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2026/0621/1579531-cape-verde-impress-again-to-earn-a-draw-with-uruguay/|title= Cape Verde impress again to earn a draw with Uruguay|date=21 June 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=26 June 2026}}</ref>
In first-half stoppage time, [[Agustín Canobbio]] put Uruguay into a 2–1 lead when he finished low to the net from six yards out after a headed pass from Araújo from the left.

In the 61st minute it was 2–2 when a mistake by [[Mathías Olivera]] trying to play the ball across his own box allowed [[Hélio Varela]] to intercept and touch the ball to the side of Uruguay goalkeeper [[Fernando Muslera]] before side footing into the empty net from outside the penalty area on the right.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cz9l5yg0885t|title= Urugua 2 Cape Verde 2|date=21 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=26 June 2026}}</ref>

===Cape Verde vs Saudi Arabia===
[[File:Hélio Varela.jpg|thumb|right|During the match between Cape Verde and Saudi Arabia.]]
The two teams had never met before.

This result makes Cape Verde the first debutant to qualify past the group stage since [[Slovakia national football team|Slovakia]] in [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010]], and the first team to do so by drawing all three games since [[Chile national football team|Chile]] in 1998. Additionally, they are only one of four debutants in the tournament to secure a spot in the round of 32.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0qylv2wdvvt|title= Cape Verde 0 Saudi Arabia 0|date=27 June 2026|work=BBC  Sport|accessdate=14 October 2026}}</ref>

In contrast, Saudi Arabia finished bottom of their group for the second consecutive World Cup, resulting in their elimination.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/27/cape-verde-saudi-arabia-world-cup-match-report|title= Cape Verde’s World Cup fairytale continues after Saudi Arabia draw secures Argentina tie|date=27 June 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=14 October 2026}}</ref>

===Uruguay vs Spain===
The teams had previously met ten times, including twice in the World Cup: a [[1950 FIFA World Cup final round#Uruguay vs Spain|2–2 final round draw]] in [[1950 FIFA World Cup|1950]] and a [[1990 FIFA World Cup Group E#Uruguay vs Spain|0–0 group stage draw]] in [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Uruguay vs. Spain Head-to-Head in the World Cups|url=https://www.thesoccerworldcups.com/head_to_head/uruguay_vs_spain.php|website=The Soccer World Cups|access-date=6 December 2025}}</ref> Their latest encounter was [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup Group B#Spain vs Uruguay|Spain's 2–1 group stage victory]] at the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup]] to keep their unbeaten head to head record.<ref>{{cite web|title=Uruguay national football team: record v Spain|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/uruguay/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Spain|website=11v11.com|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref> This was the only match in Group H played outside of the United States. Both teams returned to Mexican soil since the [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]] edition.

Uruguay's [[Agustín Canobbio]] was sent off with a straight red card. In addition, their 1–0 defeat marked the Uruguayan team's second consecutive exit from the group stage, and made it the sole South American team to fail to advance to the round of 32.

==Discipline==
The team conduct ("fair play") score would have been used as a tiebreaker if the head-to-head and overall records of teams were tied. It would also be used as a tiebreaker for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|third-place ranking]] between groups if the overall records of teams were tied. The score was calculated based on yellow and red cards received by players and team officials in all group matches as follows:<ref name="regulations"/>
*yellow card: −1 point;
*indirect red card (second yellow card): −3 points;
*direct red card: −4 points;
*yellow card and direct red card: −5 points;

Only one of the above deductions could be applied to a player or team official in a single match.
